chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abū ʿAmmār Bayyāʿ al-Aksiyah, from al-Zaydī, from Abū Arākah who said:

I heard ʿAlī (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, Allah has servants whose hearts have been broken by the awe of Allah, so they abstain from speech; and indeed they are eloquent, articulate, wise, and noble. They race towards Him with pure actions, not considering their many [good] deeds to be much, nor being satisfied with [only] little. They consider themselves to be vile, while they are truly like the sagacious and virtuous ones.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual characteristics of the humble servants of Allah according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition of *zuhd* (asceticism), this hadith highlights the paradox of the *abd al-salih*: though naturally eloquent and noble, they choose silence to preserve their hearts from distraction, viewing their abundant deeds as insufficient. This reflects the scholarly emphasis on *khushu'* (humility) and the internalization of faith, where self-effacement serves as a safeguard against spiritual pride (*ujb*).
